problem_text:
A 3D rubber bushing with a circumferential groove is loaded by a prescribed
rotation. Material: compressible neo-Hookean. The finite-element reference
uses 20-node quadratic hexahedra (Q20) on a family of globally refined meshes,
and, at one intermediate resolution, three additional meshes that cluster
elements axially toward the groove. We want to use stresses in the groove
region as reference values for validating neural-operator surrogates.
Question: which groove-region stress quantities can serve as trustworthy
validation targets, and how should that be established?

spec.name: B3 grooved rubber bushing under prescribed rotation: which groove-region stress QoIs can serve as validation targets
spec.material: Compressible neo-Hookean (finite strain). Shear and bulk moduli, and therefore the degree of near-incompressibility, are not given.
spec.loading: Prescribed rotation, applied quasi-statically as a displacement boundary condition. The rotation axis (torsional about the bushing axis or conical/tilting), its magnitude, the load-stepping and which surfaces are held fixed or rotated are not specified.
well_posedness: Boundary conditions: rigid-body motion is ruled out only if the prescribed rotation acts on one surface (for example the inner sleeve) while another surface (for example the outer sleeve) is fixed. This must be confirmed.

Bonded interfaces: where a bonded (clamped) rubber-to-sleeve interface meets a traction-free end face or the groove flank, the corner is singular (clamped-free corner). If that edge lies inside or touches the groove averaging region, even region averages can converge slowly, and maxima there will not converge.

Groove root: a rounded root with a finite radius gives a bounded stress concentration, so maxima can in principle converge, but only once the root radius is resolved by several Q20 elements. A sharp or V-shaped root gives a near-singular field, so *_max values will keep growing under refinement and cannot be validation targets. Only region averages (and energy or displacements) remain convergent.

Material stability: compressible neo-Hookean is polyconvex and stable for J > 0. Every Gauss point must keep J > 0 at the final rotation. If the bulk-to-shear ratio is large, fully integrated Q20 can lock volumetrically and pollute stresses (especially pressure-dominated sigma_ii), so the integration rule or a mixed formulation should be confirmed.

Load level: prescribed rotation (displacement control) normally avoids load-controlled limit points. Large rotations can still cause local buckling, wrinkling or self-contact of the groove flanks, which would make the solution non-unique or non-smooth. The groove faces must be confirmed to stay separated, with no contact modelled or needed.

Convergence evidence: only the global refinement family (5,040 to 47,040 elements) can show asymptotic convergence and observed order. At least 3 levels in the asymptotic range with a constant refinement ratio are needed to estimate order and a Richardson-extrapolated value. For smooth averages, Q20 should show about O(h^2) in stress.

Clustered meshes: the three z-clustering meshes at a single resolution (10,200 elements) cannot establish convergence. They are only a sensitivity check: an average is trustworthy if it is insensitive to element arrangement at fixed element count and agrees with the global family's trend. A maximum that changes strongly with axial clustering indicates a concentration or singularity that is not resolved.

Near-zero components: under pure torsion, by symmetry, some Cartesian-component averages over an axisymmetric groove region (for example sigma_xy_avg and the normal-component differences) can be close to zero. Relative error is then ill-conditioned, so absolute or norm-scaled tolerances, or the invariant sigma_frob_avg, should be used.

Proposed classification, to be confirmed by the deterministic checks: *_avg values (especially sigma_frob_avg) are candidate validation targets if they show monotone, asymptotic convergence on the global family and insensitivity to clustering. *_max values are diagnostic only and should not be used as targets unless they show convergence on both the global and clustered meshes.
open_questions: Groove root geometry: is the root filleted (what radius, and how many Q20 elements span it at each level), or sharp or V-shaped? This decides whether *_max can converge at all.
Rotation axis and magnitude (torsional vs. conical), the number of load steps, and whether results are taken only at the final load state.
Which surfaces are bonded or fixed and which are rotated? Do any bonded-to-free edges lie inside or next to the groove averaging region?
Exact definition of the 'groove region' used for *_avg and *_max (volume, axial extent, whether it includes the free groove surface), and whether the averages are volume-weighted.
Stress measure (Cauchy vs. PK1/PK2) and coordinate frame (global Cartesian vs. cylindrical). Cartesian components of a rotationally symmetric field may be poorly suited as targets.
Where are maxima evaluated: Gauss points, extrapolated nodes, or smoothed or recovered fields? This strongly affects convergence of peak values.
Material parameters: shear modulus and bulk modulus (or Poisson ratio), to judge near-incompressibility and the locking risk with Q20. Which integration rule (full or reduced) was used?
Number of levels in the global refinement family, and whether the refinement ratio is constant (5,040 to 47,040 is roughly a ratio of 2.1 in h overall, so possibly only 2 to 3 levels).
Exact form of the three z-clustering strategies (grading ratio, smallest element size at the groove compared with the finest global mesh).
Is self-contact of the groove flanks possible at the applied rotation, and was it modelled?
Solver tolerances (Newton residual) and whether they are tight enough not to dominate the discretisation error at the finest level.

checks.rationale: required by rules R2, R3, R4
required by rules R2, R3, R4

This is solution verification of the groove-region averages on the global refinement family (5,040 to 47,040 Q20 elements). These are the only candidate validation targets. gci_tol is tightened to 0.02, as the critic asked, so numerical uncertainty does not hide model-form error. The verdict is only meaningful if the family has at least 3 levels with a constant ratio. With 5,040 to 47,040 elements, h changes by only about 2.1 overall, so there are likely 2 to 3 levels, and with 2 levels the GCI rests on an assumed order. That must be confirmed. The catalogue gate uses relative tolerances only. For components that are near zero by symmetry (the Cartesian shear averages under torsion), a FAIL verdict reflects ill-conditioning, not divergence. Interpret it that way, or replace these QoIs with norm-scaled or cylindrical versions, which this catalogue cannot express.

This is diagnostic only, so that every declared QoI is covered. Peak stresses at the groove root or at bonded-to-free corners need not converge. A FAIL here confirms the maxima are unsuitable as validation targets. It cannot tell slow convergence of a resolved fillet from singular growth, so the growth trend should be reported alongside it. The same tolerances as the averages are used deliberately: a PASS would have to meet the full validation standard to count.

This checks the sensitivity of the averages to element arrangement on the three z-clustered meshes at a fixed 10,200 elements. It applies because the groove is a local feature. A PASS only shows insensitivity, not correctness. It should also be compared against the global family's trend or Richardson value, which this gate does not do. The relative-tolerance caveat for near-zero shear components applies here too.
This is diagnostic. A peak that shifts strongly under axial clustering shows a concentration or singularity that the mesh does not resolve. That supports classifying the *_max values as non-targets.

expected_failures.why: The peak sits at the groove root or at a clamped-free (bonded sleeve meeting a free face) corner, where the stress is near-singular. It keeps changing under global refinement and under z-clustering. It failed both gates in the nearest solved case.
Same mechanism as sigma_xx_max. It failed both gates in the nearest solved case.

The axial component peaks at the same groove root or bonded-edge concentration, and axial clustering directly changes how well that is resolved. Volumetric locking in fully integrated Q20, if K/mu is large, would also pollute this normal stress.
This is a shear peak at a singular or unresolved concentration, so it is not expected to converge. The root radius and how many elements resolve it are unknown.
Under torsion about the bushing axis, the dominant sigma_theta_z shear concentrates at the groove root and at bonded edges, so its Cartesian projection peaks there and grows under refinement.

It failed both qoi_convergence and strategy_robustness in the nearest solved case. This is plausible because it is a non-negative invariant: a singular contribution near the corner adds up rather than cancelling, as it can in the signed sigma_xx_avg and sigma_yy_avg, which passed. Candidate causes the gates cannot tell apart are: too few levels in the asymptotic range, the averaging region touching a clamped-free edge, or volumetric locking. This means the passing verdicts for the signed Cartesian averages should be treated with caution.

This is a likely failure that reflects ill-conditioning, not real divergence. Averaged over a full ring under torsion, the Cartesian xz and yz shear averages cancel to near zero. Small absolute changes then become large relative errors, beyond band_tol and gci_tol. This is uncertain because the rotation axis is not specified.
Same near-zero cancellation argument as sigma_xz_avg. The relative-tolerance gate is ill-conditioned.

The angular average of in-plane shear over an axisymmetric groove region is near zero by symmetry, so relative tolerances are ill-conditioned. A FAIL would not show non-convergence. This is uncertain until the rotation axis is confirmed.

objections: Self-defeating target set: sigma_frob_avg is the invariant the spec names as the main validation candidate, yet the plan lists it as an expected failure. Of the 13 QoIs, 10 are pre-declared failures. That leaves sigma_xx_avg, sigma_yy_avg and sigma_zz_avg as the only possible targets. A plan that expects its main target to fail cannot establish a validation target. It should be rebuilt around QoIs expected to pass (see missing checks) instead of being run as is.

The signed Cartesian averages cannot be accepted while sigma_frob_avg fails. The plan concedes that a passing signed average may reflect cancellation of a non-convergent local contribution rather than convergence. A PASS for sigma_xx_avg or sigma_yy_avg therefore cannot show what it claims. If the non-negative invariant fails on the same family and the same region, a signed component of that field cannot be a validation target.

Under torsion about the bushing axis, the in-plane and axial normal stresses (sigma_rr, sigma_thth and the Poynting-type sigma_zz) are second order in the twist. Their ring averages, and so sigma_xx_avg = sigma_yy_avg ≈ (sigma_rr + sigma_thth)/2 and sigma_zz_avg, may themselves be small. Relative band_tol and gci_tol at 1–2% are then ill-conditioned in the same way the plan already admits for the shear components. The plan does not address this, and the rotation axis and magnitude needed to judge it are unknown.

Running relative-tolerance gates on the near-zero shear averages (sigma_xy_avg, sigma_xz_avg, sigma_yz_avg) and labelling a FAIL in advance as 'ill-conditioning, not divergence' makes these checks unfalsifiable. A FAIL is explained away, and real divergence cannot be told apart from conditioning. These QoIs should be marked as non-targets now, or replaced by cylindrical or norm-scaled quantities. They should not be run under a gate whose verdict the plan has already decided to ignore. Under a conical or tilting rotation they would not be near zero at all, so the expected-failure rationale itself depends on an unresolved open question.

Two global levels are not enough. 5,040 to 47,040 elements in 3D is an overall h-ratio of about 9.33^(1/3) ≈ 2.1, so there are probably only 2–3 levels. With 2 levels the GCI rests on an assumed order and observed convergence is never shown. The plan says this 'must be confirmed' but still runs the gate unconditionally. The level count and the constant ratio must be a precondition for any convergence verdict, not a caveat in the rationale.

There is no check that the observed order is near the theoretical value. Q20 stress for a smooth field should converge at about O(h^2). An average reaching a 2% GCI with, for example, an observed p of about 0.5 or 4 shows it is not in the asymptotic range, or that a singularity or locking is polluting it. The plan never compares the observed order against the expected one.

strategy_robustness at a single 10,200-element resolution, below the finest global level, only shows that the result is insensitive to element arrangement at a coarse-to-intermediate resolution. Three meshes agreeing within 2% at that size can all share the same discretisation error. Without comparing against the global family's Richardson value (which the plan admits this gate does not do), a PASS gives no evidence of correctness and should not count toward target status.

The expected failures are justified mainly by 'failed in the nearest solved case', not by the theory for this geometry. Because the root radius, bonded edges and averaging region are all unknown, these predictions are not tied to the mechanism in this problem. Tuning the plan to match a neighbouring case's outcomes risks circular confirmation. The singular-contribution explanation for sigma_frob_avg is also speculative. In 3D, an integrable edge singularity gives a finite region average that converges, only at a reduced rate. Persistent failure therefore points more to pre-asymptotic levels, locking or region definition than to the invariant 'adding up' the singularity.

The well-posedness preconditions decide whether any average can converge, and they are unresolved. Does the averaging region touch a bonded-to-free edge? Is the groove root filleted or sharp? Which surfaces are fixed or rotated (ruling out rigid-body motion)? Does J stay > 0 at every Gauss point? Is there locking given the unknown K/mu and integration rule? Do the groove flanks come into self-contact? Running verdicts first and interpreting them later is not acceptable for a validation target.

Stress measure and frame are unspecified. Under a prescribed finite rotation, global-Cartesian Cauchy components mix through the rigid rotation of material points. That makes component averages frame-dependent and physically awkward targets. The targets should be the invariant (Frobenius or von Mises) or cylindrical components, with the stress measure (Cauchy vs. PK2) stated.

The maxima diagnostics are acceptable as non-targets, but their verdicts depend on where peaks are sampled (Gauss points, extrapolated nodes or recovered fields), which is unspecified. Also, a single PASS on a 2-level family must not promote any *_max value to a target.
missing_checks: Precondition gate: confirm the global family has at least 3 levels in the asymptotic range with a constant refinement ratio. Refuse convergence or GCI verdicts otherwise.
Observed-order check for every *_avg QoI: observed p compared against the expected Q20 stress order (about 2 for smooth averages). Flag p far below or above it as pre-asymptotic or polluted.

Convergence of global, well-posed QoIs that do not depend on the groove-root singularity: strain energy, reaction torque or moment at the rotated surface, and representative displacements. These are the natural validation targets and are currently absent.
Compare each clustered-mesh *_avg value against the global family's Richardson-extrapolated value, not only for agreement among the three clustered meshes.
J > 0 at every Gauss point at the final load step, on all meshes.
Volumetric locking assessment: state K/mu and the integration rule, and compare full vs. reduced integration (or a mixed formulation) for pressure-dominated sigma_ii averages and sigma_frob_avg.
Confirm the boundary conditions (which surface is rotated and which is fixed) and the rotation axis and magnitude, before deciding which components are near zero by symmetry.
Check the averaging region geometry: show that the groove region does not include or touch a bonded-to-free (clamped-free) edge, or quantify the effect of shrinking or offsetting the region.

Groove root resolution: give the fillet radius and the number of Q20 elements spanning it at each level, or state that the root is sharp. This decides whether the *_max diagnostics can converge at all.
Self-contact and wrinkling check on the groove flanks at the final rotation.
Newton residual tolerance at the finest level shown to be well below the discretisation error.

Replace the Cartesian component QoIs with cylindrical components (sigma_rr, sigma_thth, sigma_zz, sigma_thz) or norm-scaled absolute tolerances for components that are near zero by symmetry or second order in the twist, and state the stress measure.

per_qoi.interpretation: Oscillatory on the finest three (0.936, 0.898, 0.910; norm-scaled spread 4.2%) and 16.7% spread across z-clustering strategies. The Frobenius norm is non-negative, so local concentrations inside the averaging region (groove root and/or clamped-free corners) count fully and do not cancel. Not a validation target, which contradicts the spec's proposed primary target. Most likely driven by the non-converged shear component sigma_xz.

Finest three within the 1% band (0.31%, norm-scaled) and insensitive to element arrangement (0.79%). The sequence oscillates, so no observed order or Richardson-extrapolated value is available. Usable as a validation target with roughly band-level numerical uncertainty.
Within band (0.27%) and strategy-robust (0.87%). Same caveat as xx: band-based acceptance, no asymptotic order demonstrated.

Marginal pass: 0.87% norm-scaled spread (about 1.9% relative to its own value), oscillatory, 1.3% clustering spread. Weakest of the normal-component passes. If the material is nearly incompressible, the pressure-dominated normal stresses are the most exposed to Q20 volumetric locking, which the gates do not test.

Near zero (about -8.7e-4 against a stress scale of about 0.91). It passes because its magnitude is negligible under the norm-scaled tolerance. Its own relative variation is about 8%. Can only be stated as 'approximately zero' with an absolute tolerance, not as a converged value.

Dominant shear average (about -0.31). Oscillatory (3.9% spread) and clustering-sensitive (3.9%). The averaging region likely includes an unresolved concentration that affects shear. Large xz with near-zero yz implies the load or region is not axisymmetric torsion about z. The rotation axis and region definition must be clarified.
Near zero (about -0.012). Passes under the norm-scaled tolerance, but its own relative variation is about 8%. Report only as small, with an absolute tolerance.

Oscillatory, 20% spread, 23% clustering spread. Peak not resolved. Consistent with a stress concentration or singularity that the meshes do not resolve, and/or the location of the maximum jumping between evaluation points. Diagnostic only.
Oscillatory, 11% spread, 40% clustering spread. Peak not resolved. Diagnostic only.

Oscillatory, 15% spread, 57% clustering spread, the strongest sensitivity to axial clustering. Points to an unresolved concentration or near-singularity at the groove (sharp root, or a clamped-free edge). Diagnostic only.

Passes only because its magnitude (about 0.02) is small against the norm scale. Its own variation across the finest three is about 40%. Not a resolved peak and must not be used as a validation target, consistent with the spec's rule that maxima are diagnostic.

Monotone decrease but observed order 0.20 and GCI_fine 379% against a 2% tolerance, far below the roughly O(h^2) expected for Q20 stresses in smooth regions. This is the signature of a near-singular peak that will not converge under refinement. Diagnostic only.
Small magnitude (about 0.04), oscillatory, about 11% variation relative to itself. Passes only under the norm-scaled tolerance. Not a validation target.

advice.summary: Spreads are scaled by the global stress level (about 0.91, i.e. the sigma_frob_avg magnitude), so PASS verdicts on near-zero components (sigma_xy_avg, sigma_yz_avg, sigma_xy_max, sigma_yz_max) mean 'negligible relative to the stress scale', not converged. The only substantive passes are the normal-stress averages sigma_xx_avg, sigma_yy_avg and sigma_zz_avg. They are accepted by a 1% band with oscillatory sequences, so no observed order or extrapolated value is available, and sigma_zz_avg is marginal. The dominant shear average sigma_xz_avg and the invariant sigma_frob_avg FAIL on both convergence and clustering robustness. This suggests that an unresolved concentration lies inside the groove averaging region, and it contradicts the spec's plan to use sigma_frob_avg as the primary target. All substantive maxima fail (oscillation, 11-57% clustering sensitivity, and an observed order of 0.20 for sigma_xz_max), which fits a sharp groove root or clamped-free corners. Interpretation remains conditional on unresolved open questions: root geometry, bonded edges near the region, rotation axis (large xz with near-zero yz argues against pure torsion about z), region definition, number of levels, material parameters and integration rule (locking risk for sigma_zz).
advice.manuscript_wording: For the grooved bushing under prescribed rotation, groove-region stress quantities were assessed on a global refinement family (5,040 to 47,040 Q20 elements) and on three axially clustered meshes of 10,200 elements each. Acceptance tolerances were scaled by the overall stress magnitude. Only the region-averaged normal Cauchy stress components sigma_xx, sigma_yy and sigma_zz met both criteria: the three finest global meshes agreed to within 1% of the stress scale, and the results were insensitive to element clustering. Their mesh sequences were non-monotone, so no convergence order or extrapolated value is claimed, and they are reported with an estimated numerical uncertainty of about 1%. The region-averaged xy and yz shear components are negligible relative to the stress scale and are reported only as approximately zero. The region-averaged xz shear stress and the averaged Frobenius norm of stress did not converge and were sensitive to mesh clustering. This indicates an unresolved stress concentration within the averaging region, so neither is used as a validation target. Peak stress components did not converge (for example, sigma_xz_max shows an observed order of about 0.2) or were sensitive to mesh arrangement by up to 57%. Peaks that formally met the tolerance are small in magnitude and vary substantially relative to their own values. No peak stress is therefore used for validation, and peak values are presented as qualitative indicators of the stress concentration at the groove only.
